books.section: The Decline of Public Trust in the 1970s

primary_sources: Jimmy Carter, televised address, July 15, 1979 (paraphrased); Torrijos-Carter Treaties, 1977

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from Carter's record, 1977-1979

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of President Jimmy Carter's 1976 campaign promise, the Panama Canal treaties of 1977, and his televised address of July 15, 1979. Account drawn from the grounding books (Barron's Ch. 10, Topic 8.14; 5 Steps Ch. 28; Princeton Ch. 12).
stimulus.text: Paraphrase of President Jimmy Carter's record in 1977-1979. Carter won the presidency in 1976 as a Washington outsider who promised, 'I will never lie to you.' In 1977 he signed treaties returning the Panama Canal Zone to Panama by December 31, 1999. On July 15, 1979, in a televised address, he said the country faced a 'crisis of confidence' that went deeper than the energy shortage, and he called for sacrifice and conservation.

options.text: Outsiders always govern easily once they are elected to the White House.
options.misconception: Background: Carter's outsider style hurt him with Congress, so outsiders do not always govern easily.

options.text: Voters liked an honest outsider after Watergate, but Congress resented his scorn.
Carter had served many terms in Congress before running in 1976.
options.misconception: Background: Carter had been governor of Georgia, not a member of Congress.

options.text: Voters in 1976 wanted a career Washington politician in the White House.
options.misconception: Carter won as an outsider who promised he would never lie. Background: After Watergate, voters wanted the opposite of the dishonesty they had seen.

rationales.A: Background: Carter's outsider style hurt him with Congress, so outsiders do not always govern easily.
rationales.B: Background: Carter won by promising honesty after Watergate, but even congressional Democrats resented his scorn for Washington politics, which hurt his governing.
rationales.C: Background: Carter had been governor of Georgia, not a member of Congress.
rationales.D: Carter won as an outsider who promised he would never lie. Background: After Watergate, voters wanted the opposite of the dishonesty they had seen.
rationales.general:
1. The passage says Carter won as an outsider who promised he would never lie.
2. Background: After Watergate, voters wanted honesty, so the outsider promise won the election.
3. Background: That same scorn for Washington politics hurt him with Congress once he had to govern.
Remember: The quality that wins an election can be the quality that makes governing hard.
